title: KDP File Upload Failed? Here's Every Possible Cause
description: Amazon KDP file upload failed, froze, or never completed? Learn every common cause and fix for KDP manuscript upload failed, cover upload failed, PDF upload errors, browser problems, file size issues, filenames, corrupted PDFs, and KDP settings.
metaTitle: KDP File Upload Failed? Every Cause and Fix

excerpt: If your KDP file upload fails, freezes, or gets stuck before Previewer opens, the cause is usually file format, file size, browser state, internet timeout, filename, corrupted PDF, or mismatched KDP settings. This guide shows how to find and fix it.

shortAnswer: A KDP file upload failed error usually means the file did not complete transfer or could not pass the first processing stage. Common causes include wrong file format, oversized PDFs, corrupted exports, browser cache, extensions, unstable internet, VPNs, special characters in filenames, complex transparency, and KDP setup mismatches.

relatedGuides.label: Why Amazon KDP Keeps Rejecting My PDF

faqs.question: Why does my KDP upload stop at 99%?
faqs.answer: A KDP upload that stops at 99% usually completed most of the transfer but failed during final handoff, storage, or early validation. The most common causes are a large PDF, unstable internet, browser cache problems, extensions, VPN interference, or a PDF that KDP struggles to process. Try a clean browser first, then rename and re-export the PDF if the problem repeats.

faqs.question: Can a PDF be too large for KDP?
faqs.answer: Yes. KDP can process large files, but very large PDFs are more likely to upload slowly, time out, freeze, or fail during validation. This is common with coloring books, photo books, and Canva files built from huge PNG pages. Optimize source images to the final print size, flatten finished pages, and avoid unnecessary transparency before export.

faqs.question: Does KDP support Canva PDFs?
faqs.answer: KDP can accept Canva PDFs when they are exported correctly and match KDP's print requirements. Use PDF Print, correct custom dimensions, proper bleed when needed, and simple filenames. Canva PDFs fail when they use the wrong size, Standard PDF export, missing bleed, huge images, visible crop marks, or complex transparent layers.

faqs.question: Can browser extensions cause KDP upload failures?
faqs.answer: Yes. Browser extensions can interfere with KDP pages, upload scripts, cookies, session storage, and file transfer behavior. Ad blockers, privacy tools, download managers, translation extensions, and security add-ons are common suspects. Test in an incognito window with extensions disabled or use another browser before rebuilding the book file.

faqs.question: Can a filename break a KDP upload?
faqs.answer: Yes. Filenames with emoji, unusual Unicode symbols, punctuation, very long names, or special characters can cause upload problems. Use a simple lowercase filename with hyphens, such as book-title-interior.pdf or book-title-cover.pdf. This will not fix a bad PDF, but it removes one easy failure point.

faqs.question: Why does KDP upload work on another browser?
faqs.answer: If the same file uploads in another browser, the file may not be the main problem. The original browser may have stale cache, blocked cookies, extension conflicts, session errors, or memory pressure. Continue the upload in the working browser, then clear cache and disable extensions in the browser that failed.

faqs.question: Can VPNs cause KDP upload failures?
faqs.answer: Yes. VPNs can slow upload speed, create unstable routes, trigger security checks, or interrupt large file transfers. Corporate firewalls and public Wi-Fi networks can create similar problems. If a KDP upload keeps timing out, test from a stable home connection without VPN, proxy, or aggressive firewall filtering.

faqs.question: Why does upload fail but preview never starts?
faqs.answer: If upload fails before Previewer starts, KDP probably never finished receiving or storing the file. That is different from Previewer not loading, where upload completes but rendering stalls. Check file format, filename, browser, internet stability, and file size first. If upload completes but Previewer freezes, move to PDF processing and optimization checks.

faqs.question: Should I use PDF Standard or PDF Print from Canva for KDP?
faqs.answer: Use PDF Print for KDP print books. PDF Standard is meant for lighter digital sharing and may reduce quality or alter output in ways that are not ideal for print. PDF Print still needs the correct dimensions and bleed setup; it does not automatically make a wrong-size design KDP-ready.

faqs.question: How do I know if KDP itself is temporarily broken?
faqs.answer: Test with a small known-good PDF, try another browser, check your connection, and wait before rebuilding files. If multiple unrelated files fail, KDP pages are slow, or other creators report issues, it may be temporary. If only one file fails repeatedly, assume the file or local browser environment is the cause.

summary: A KDP upload failure is different from a PDF rejection or approval rejection; it often happens before Previewer or review begins.
The most common causes are wrong format, large files, corrupted PDFs, browser state, internet timeouts, filenames, transparency, and mismatched KDP settings.
A systematic workflow is faster than guessing: check format, file size, filename, browser, PDF health, internet, KDP settings, then re-upload.
checklist: Rename the file with simple lowercase letters and hyphens.
Remove special characters, emoji, and unusual symbols from the filename.
Re-export the PDF from the source file.
Check upload speed and internet stability.
Turn off VPN or proxy temporarily.
Verify the file format is accepted by KDP.
Check trim size and bleed settings.
Flatten complex transparency in the upload copy.
Remove crop marks and visible template layers unless required.
Test a smaller PDF if the upload keeps timing out.
Run the final file through a preflight check before uploading again.

howTo.name: How to fix a KDP file upload failed error
howTo.description: A step-by-step workflow for diagnosing KDP file uploads that fail, freeze, time out, or never complete.

steps.name: Rule out browser and network problems
steps.text: Try another browser, disable extensions, clear cache, and test from a stable connection without VPN.

steps.name: Check filename and file format
steps.text: Rename the file with simple lowercase letters and hyphens, then confirm the manuscript or cover is in a KDP-supported format.

steps.name: Inspect file size and PDF health
steps.text: If the file is large or image-heavy, optimize images, flatten finished pages, and re-export a fresh PDF from the source file.

steps.name: Verify KDP book settings
steps.text: Confirm trim size, bleed, paperback or hardcover format, paper type, and cover/interior dimensions are consistent.

steps.name: Upload the clean file again
steps.text: Use the fresh export, keep the browser session clean, and upload again after validating the file.

content: You upload a KDP cover. The progress bar reaches 20%, then stops. Or you upload a manuscript and KDP instantly displays an upload error. You try again. Same result. You start wondering whether Amazon KDP is broken.
Sometimes it is. KDP can have temporary delays. Browsers can behave badly. Internet connections can drop at exactly the wrong moment.

But most repeated KDP file upload failed errors come from something more specific: a file KDP cannot receive cleanly, store reliably, validate quickly, or process into Previewer. That could be file size, format, corruption, filename, browser state, internet timeout, transparency, or a book setup mismatch.
This guide walks through every likely cause and the order to test them, so you do not waste hours re-uploading the same file.
## Quick Fix Checklist
Start here before rebuilding your whole book:
- Try another browser.
- Rename the file.
- Remove special characters from the filename.
- Reduce file size if the PDF is image-heavy.
- Re-export the PDF from the source file.
- Clear browser cache and cookies.
- Disable browser extensions.
- Check your internet connection and upload speed.
- Verify the file format is correct.
- Try the upload again from a clean browser session.
If one of these fixes works, you have learned something useful. If none work, continue through the deeper file and KDP configuration checks below.
## What Does "Upload Failed" Actually Mean?
Upload failed does not always mean KDP rejected your book. It often means KDP did not complete the file transfer or could not move the file into the next processing stage.
That is different from Previewer failing, PDF rejection, or approval rejection. Each stage points to a different class of problem.
| Message or symptom | Where it happens | What it usually means | First place to check |
| Upload failed | During transfer | Browser, internet, file size, format, filename | Browser and file basics |
| Upload stuck | During transfer or storage | Large file, slow connection, KDP delay | File size and network |
| Previewer failed | After upload completes | KDP cannot render proof | PDF complexity and dimensions |
| PDF rejected | Validation stage | File fails print requirements | Trim, bleed, fonts, resolution |
| Approval rejected | After review | Content, metadata, quality, or policy issue | KDP message and book setup |
If the upload never completes, do not start with content policy or cover design. Start with transfer, browser, filename, format, and PDF health.

For validation failures after upload completes, use [Why Amazon KDP Keeps Rejecting My PDF](/blog/why-amazon-kdp-keeps-rejecting-my-pdf). For Previewer-specific freezes, use [KDP Previewer Not Loading](/blog/kdp-previewer-not-loading).
## How Amazon KDP Upload Processing Works

KDP upload processing is a pipeline. Your browser sends the file to Amazon. Amazon stores it. KDP validates the file structure. Then it generates Previewer output. Later, the book goes through review before approval.
A failure can happen at any stage:
1. Upload: the browser cannot complete the transfer.
2. Storage: KDP receives the file but cannot finalize it.
3. Validation: KDP checks file format, dimensions, fonts, and PDF structure.
4. Preview generation: KDP renders the manuscript and cover for inspection.
5. Review: KDP checks book quality, metadata, and publishing requirements.

The official [KDP print book formatting guidelines](https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G201857950), [cover formatting guidance](https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G201834180), and [cover calculator/templates](https://kdp.amazon.com/cover-calculator) are useful references when an upload failure turns out to be a file setup problem.
## Cause #1: Wrong File Format

KDP expects specific file formats depending on what you upload. A print manuscript is usually a PDF. A print cover is commonly a PDF cover file or a supported image in certain workflows. Ebooks have their own accepted formats.

Common mistakes include uploading a Canva project file instead of an exported PDF, uploading a ZIP, uploading screenshots, uploading a corrupted PDF renamed from another extension, or trying to use a file type that belongs to ebook publishing for a print book.

How to identify it: check the file extension and open the exported file in a normal PDF viewer. Make sure the upload slot in KDP matches the file you are uploading: manuscript to manuscript, cover to cover.

How to fix it: return to the source app and export the correct file type. For Canva, use PDF Print for print books. For professional design apps, use a print PDF preset and verify dimensions after export.
## Cause #2: File Size Too Large

Large files are one of the biggest causes of stuck or failed KDP uploads. This is especially common with coloring books, photo books, puzzle books, journals with full-page art, and image-heavy Canva exports.

A file can be too heavy because images are far larger than their final print size, pages are built from transparent PNGs, the PDF contains live effects, or the same heavy asset is repeated across many pages. A 400 MB PDF may open locally but still fail during browser upload or KDP processing.
How to reduce file size safely:
- Resize images to about 300 DPI at final print size.
- Flatten finished pages where transparency is not needed.
- Avoid giant PNGs for simple black-and-white pages.
- Replace screenshots with original artwork or text.
- Export one clean PDF from the source file instead of repeated conversions.
- Avoid aggressive compression that blurs line art or photos.
If your PDF uploads but takes forever to process, see [KDP PDF Upload Takes Forever](/blog/kdp-pdf-upload-takes-forever).
## Cause #3: Corrupted PDF
A corrupted PDF does not always look broken. It may open in Preview or Acrobat while still failing when KDP tries to receive, validate, or render it.

Symptoms include immediate upload failure, repeated failure at the same percentage, Previewer never starting, or the problem disappearing after a fresh export. Causes include incomplete exports, damaged fonts, converter chains, broken page boxes, unsupported transparency, or a PDF saved through too many tools.

How to verify: open the PDF properties, check page dimensions, scan a few pages, and try uploading a small known-good PDF. If the known-good PDF uploads but your book does not, the issue is likely inside the file.
How to repair: return to the original source file, export a fresh PDF with a new filename, avoid online converter chains, embed fonts, flatten finished effects, and test again.
## Cause #4: Browser Problems
KDP is a web app, so your browser matters. Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge can behave differently depending on cache, cookies, extensions, memory, hardware acceleration, and security settings.

Extensions can interfere with uploads. Privacy tools can block scripts. Ad blockers can alter page behavior. Download managers can hook into file handling. Old cookies can break an active KDP session.
Fix workflow:
1. Try Chrome or Edge first.
2. Open an incognito or private window.
3. Disable extensions.
4. Clear KDP-related cache and cookies.
5. Restart the browser.
6. Try the upload again.
If upload works in another browser, the file may be fine. Continue with the working browser and clean up the failing one later.
## Cause #5: Internet Upload Timeout
Large uploads need stable upstream bandwidth. Download speed is not the same as upload speed. A connection that streams video well can still have poor upload stability.

Timeouts are more likely on public Wi-Fi, mobile hotspots, VPNs, corporate networks, hotel networks, or connections with packet loss. KDP may appear stuck because the browser is still trying to finish a transfer that the network keeps interrupting.
How to identify it: run an upload speed test, try a smaller PDF, and test from another network. If small files upload but large files fail, network or file size is likely involved.

How to fix it: use a stable home connection, disable VPN temporarily, avoid public Wi-Fi, close bandwidth-heavy apps, and upload during a quieter time. If you must use a slow connection, reduce file size safely first.
## Cause #6: Filename Problems
Filenames should be boring. KDP uploads are not the place for emoji, unusual symbols, long punctuation-heavy names, or mixed-language special characters.
Risky examples:
- My Book Final!!!.pdf
- cover ❤️ version 2.pdf
- manuscript(NEW)#1.pdf
- KDP upload – final – really final.pdf
Better examples:
- book-title-interior.pdf
- book-title-cover.pdf
- coloring-book-manuscript-v2.pdf
Spaces usually work in many systems, but hyphens are cleaner. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. Keep the filename short and descriptive.
## Cause #7: Transparency and Complex Layers

Design-heavy PDFs can contain transparent PNGs, shadows, masks, blend modes, hidden layers, and live effects. KDP may struggle to upload, validate, or render those files, especially when the same complexity appears on many pages.

Canva files can become heavy when pages include transparent elements and repeated backgrounds. Illustrator and InDesign files can carry complex vector effects. Photoshop files can export huge raster pages if smart objects and layers are not managed.
Flattening workflow:
1. Keep an editable master file.
2. Duplicate it for upload export.
3. Remove hidden template layers and old objects.
4. Flatten finished effects that do not need to stay live.
5. Export a clean print PDF.
6. Inspect the final PDF before upload.
Flatten the upload copy, not your only editable file.
## Cause #8: Wrong KDP Book Configuration

Sometimes the upload appears to fail because the file and KDP setup disagree. The manuscript might be built for one trim size while KDP is set to another. The cover might be for paperback while the project is hardcover. The paper type may have changed, which changes spine width. The bleed setting may not match the PDF dimensions.

How to identify it: compare trim size, paperback or hardcover format, ink and paper type, bleed setting, manuscript page count, and cover template size. If the cover was designed before the manuscript was final, recalculate it.

How to fix it: update the KDP setup or rebuild the file so both agree. For edge placement and bleed decisions, use [KDP Bleed vs No Bleed](/blog/kdp-bleed-vs-no-bleed), [KDP Safe Area Explained](/blog/kdp-safe-area-explained), and [KDP Margin Too Small Error](/blog/fix-kdp-margin-too-small-error).
## Cause #9: Temporary Amazon KDP Issues
KDP can have temporary server delays, maintenance, regional routing issues, or upload instability. You should consider this possibility, but only after a basic sanity check.

Signs it may be KDP: multiple unrelated files fail, KDP pages load slowly, a small known-good file also fails, other creators report issues, or the same file uploaded successfully recently and nothing changed.

Before changing files, try another browser, another network, and a small test PDF. If everything fails, wait and retry later. If only one file fails repeatedly, assume the file or local upload environment is the cause.
## Coloring Book Creator Problems
Coloring books are upload-failure magnets because they often combine high page count, full-page artwork, black backgrounds, patterns, and large repeated images.

A color-by-number book may include hundreds of tiny labels. A mosaic book may contain dense vector or raster patterns. A black-background coloring book may use full-page ink coverage. A Canva coloring book may place one huge PNG per page.

The fix is not to destroy quality. The fix is to size images correctly, flatten pages when appropriate, avoid unnecessary transparency, and keep the PDF efficient. Line art should stay crisp, but it does not need to be built from enormous transparent canvases.
## Canva User Upload Problems
Canva users most often run into wrong export type, wrong dimensions, missing bleed, visible crop marks, transparency-heavy pages, and oversized image assets.

Use PDF Print for KDP print books. PDF Standard is lighter but not the right default for print upload. If your book needs bleed, turn on bleed view and extend backgrounds beyond trim. If it does not need bleed, keep content inside margins and do not force edge-to-edge art.

Crop marks are usually not needed for KDP uploads unless a specific workflow calls for them. They can make the PDF dimensions or visible content confusing. Export clean, inspect the PDF properties, then upload.
For the full Canva workflow, see [Canva to KDP Export Settings](/blog/canva-to-kdp-export-settings).
## The Complete Troubleshooting Flowchart
Use this order when KDP upload fails:
1. Upload failed.
2. Check file format.
3. Check file size.
4. Check filename.
5. Check browser.
6. Check PDF health.
7. Check internet connection.
8. Check KDP book settings.
9. Re-export if needed.
10. Upload again.
Do not start by redesigning the cover if the browser is the problem. Do not start by clearing cache if the PDF is 600 MB. The order matters.
## How KDPPreflight Helps

KDPPreflight helps by inspecting the final upload file before you give it to Amazon. It can help with file inspection, dimension validation, PDF checks, bleed validation, trim validation, safe-area risk, spine width, and print-readiness signals.

It does not promise approval. KDP is the final validator, and Amazon can update requirements. But a preflight check gives you a practical way to catch common file problems before another slow upload attempt.
Use it after export. KDP analyzes the PDF you upload, not the Canva canvas or design source file.
## Prevent Future Upload Failures
Before every KDP upload, use this 15-point checklist:
- Export the correct file format.
- Use a simple filename.
- Avoid emoji and special characters.
- Check PDF page dimensions.
- Match trim size in KDP.
- Match bleed setting in KDP.
- Optimize oversized images.
- Flatten finished transparency.
- Remove hidden template layers.
- Embed fonts where needed.
- Keep the browser clean.
- Disable extensions for upload.
- Use a stable internet connection.
- Avoid VPN during large uploads.
- Preflight the final file before upload.
## Conclusion
Most KDP upload failures come from a small group of causes: file size, file format, PDF corruption, browser issues, filenames, internet instability, transparency, or KDP configuration mismatch.
The frustrating part is that KDP may only say upload failed. The productive response is to troubleshoot the upload stage first, then the file, then the book setup.

Work through the checklist once, calmly. Rename the file, test a clean browser, check the connection, verify format, optimize and re-export the PDF, then upload again. That systematic approach solves far more KDP upload problems than repeatedly pressing the same upload button and hoping the next attempt behaves differently.
